Core idea: Linear and sequential. Each phase finishes before the next starts. Changes late in the project are costly.
Terms to know: Requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance. Predictive. Heavy documentation.

Core idea: Iterative and incremental delivery of working product, with customer feedback every cycle.
Terms to know: Sprint/iteration, backlog, self-organizing team, adaptive planning, continuous improvement, deliver value early.

Core idea: Agile framework using time-boxed sprints (commonly 2 to 4 weeks, never longer than 1 month in the Scrum Guide).
Terms to know: Roles: Product Owner (maximizes value, owns product backlog), Scrum Master (facilitator, removes impediments), Development Team (builds the increment). Events: sprint planning, daily scrum/stand-up, sprint review, sprint retrospective. Artifacts: product backlog, sprint backlog, increment.

Core idea: Visual pull system. Cards move across columns on a board.
Terms to know: Visualize work, limit work in progress (WIP), manage flow, cycle time, throughput, continuous delivery with no fixed iterations.

Core idea: Agile engineering practices for high-quality code.
Terms to know: Pair programming (driver and observer), test-driven development (TDD), continuous integration, simple design, refactoring, small releases, collective code ownership, on-site customer.

Core idea: Applies Agile and Lean at enterprise scale.
Terms to know: Agile Release Train (ART, 50 to 125 people), Program Increment (PI, about 8 to 12 weeks), Lean Portfolio Management, Portfolio Kanban.

Core idea: Joins development and operations to shorten delivery with automation and shared ownership.
Terms to know: Continuous integration (CI), continuous delivery/deployment (CD), infrastructure as code (IaC), monitoring and feedback, breaking down silos.

Core idea: DevOps with security built into every stage.
Terms to know: Shift left (test security early), security as code, automated security testing, threat modeling, continuous monitoring.

Core idea: Process-based, stage-by-stage method with strong governance.
Terms to know: 7 principles (continued business justification, learn from experience, defined roles, manage by stages, manage by exception, focus on products, tailor to suit). 7 themes (business case, organization, quality, plans, risk, change, progress). 7 processes (starting up, initiating, directing, controlling a stage, managing product delivery, managing stage boundaries, closing). Project Board, product-based planning.

Core idea: The phases software goes through, regardless of method.
Terms to know: Planning, analysis, design, implementation/coding, testing, deployment, maintenance and support. Documentation, review and evaluation, and feedback and iteration run through every phase, and iterative models loop back to earlier phases. Closure ends it with a post-implementation review.
